clues.clue: I left Ur of the Chaldees.
clues.concern: Lot also left Ur of the Chaldees with Terah and Abram (Genesis 11:31), so this clue alone fits the distractor Lot.

clues.clue: God changed my name.
clues.concern: God also changed Jacob's name to Israel (Genesis 32:28; 35:10), so this clue alone fits the distractor Jacob.

clues.clue: My wife laughed at God's promise of a son.
God tested me in the land of Moriah.
clues.concern: KJV says God did 'tempt' Abraham; 'tested' is an accurate modern gloss.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (leaving Ur) also fits Lot (Genesis 11:31). Clue 2 (God changed my name) also fits Jacob (Genesis 32:28; 35:10). Taken together, the clues point only to Abraham.
notes: The answer, Abraham, is correct and uniquely determined by the full set of clues, especially clues 3 and 4. However, two early clues individually apply to distractors. Consider rewording them to be Abraham-specific: 'The LORD brought me out of Ur of the Chaldees' (Gen 15:7) and 'God changed my name from Abram' (Gen 17:5). The explanation accurately reflects Genesis 22:1-2.

clues.clue: I was formed of the dust of the ground.
I gave names to the animals.
I lived in the garden of Eden.
My wife was Eve.
clues.concern: Genesis 3:20 names Eve but does not use the word 'wife'. Genesis 4:1 ('Adam knew Eve his wife') states the relationship explicitly and could be cited as well.

notes: The marked answer, Adam, is correct. None of the distractors fits any clue. Enoch, Cain and Seth were born to mortal parents, did not name the animals, and lived outside Eden. Cain and Seth were children of Eve, not her husbands. The explanation quotes Genesis 2:20 accurately, and that verse falls within the cited range of 2:19-20.

clues.clue: I was a tiller of the ground.
God did not respect my offering.
I asked: Am I my brother's keeper?
God set a mark upon me.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV and point uniquely to Cain. Abel was a keeper of sheep whose offering was respected. Seth and Lamech fit none of the clues. Lamech mentions Cain's sevenfold vengeance in Genesis 4:24, but no mark is set on Lamech. The explanation matches Genesis 4:9.

clues.clue: I was a mighty man of wealth in Bethlehem.
clues.concern: Ruth 2:1 calls Boaz 'a mighty man of wealth' but does not name Bethlehem. That link comes from Ruth 2:4 ('Boaz came from Bethlehem').

clues.clue: I let a Moabite woman glean in my fields.
I redeemed the inheritance of Elimelech.
clues.concern: KJV says 'bought all that was Elimelech's'. Calling this 'redeemed' fits the redemption context of Ruth 4:4-6, so it is acceptable.

clues.clue: I married Ruth.

notes: Boaz is correct, and the explanation quotes Ruth 4:13 accurately. Elimelech, Obed and Jesse are all from Bethlehem, but none of the clues fits them as a whole. The first clue's reference to Bethlehem is supported by Ruth 2:4 rather than Ruth 2:1.

clues.clue: My name is interpreted 'the son of consolation'.
clues.concern: Strictly, it is the surname 'Barnabas' given by the apostles (his given name was Joses) that is interpreted this way. This is minor, but 'My surname' would be more precise.

clues.clue: I sold land and laid the money at the apostles' feet.
I brought Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem.
I travelled with Paul on his first missionary journey.
clues.concern: This clue also partly fits Mark (John Mark), who went with Paul and Barnabas as their minister (Acts 13:5) before departing at Perga (Acts 13:13). The other clues still identify Barnabas uniquely.

distractor_conflict: Clue 4 partly fits Mark (Acts 13:5, 13), who accompanied Paul and Barnabas on part of the first journey.
notes: The answer and the explanation are accurate to Acts 4:36-37. Two optional refinements: reword clue 1 to say 'My surname given by the apostles' to match the text. Reword clue 4 to 'I was sent out with Saul from Antioch by the Holy Ghost' (Acts 13:2-4), which avoids the overlap with Mark.

clues.clue: I was the youngest son of Jesse.
clues.concern: KJV 1 Samuel 16:11 says 'There remaineth yet the youngest' and 17:14 says 'David was the youngest'; 1 Chronicles 2:15 lists David as the seventh son. The clue is fully supported.

clues.clue: I played the harp for King Saul.
I defeated Goliath.
clues.concern: 2 Samuel 21:19 in the KJV credits Elhanan with slaying 'the brother of Goliath' (the italics show those words were added by the translators). This does not fit any distractor.

clues.clue: I became king over Israel.
clues.concern: Saul and Solomon also became king over Israel. On its own this clue fits two distractors, but the earlier clues make the answer unambiguous.

distractor_conflict: The clue 'I became king over Israel' also fits Saul (1 Samuel 11:15) and Solomon (1 Kings 1:39; 1 Kings 4:1). The other clues single out David.
notes: The answer David is correct, and the explanation accurately paraphrases 1 Samuel 16:23. The fourth clue is generic and shared by two distractors, but the item as a whole is unambiguous. Consider making it more specific, e.g. 'I reigned in Hebron, then over all Israel' (2 Samuel 5:4-5).

clues.clue: I was taken captive to Babylon as a young man.
clues.concern: The KJV calls Daniel and his companions 'children' (youths), so 'young man' is a fair paraphrase. Ezekiel was also a captive in Babylon (Ezekiel 1:1-3), but his age is not stated, so this clue only partly overlaps with a distractor.

clues.clue: I purposed not to defile myself with the king's meat.
I read the writing on the wall.
clues.concern: Daniel 5:17 is where Daniel promises to read the writing. The reading and interpretation itself is in Daniel 5:25-28.

clues.clue: I was delivered from the den of lions.

notes: The marked answer, Daniel, is correct, and the explanation matches Daniel 6:23. Clue 1 alone could loosely suggest Ezekiel, since he was also a Babylonian exile, but clues 2-4 point only to Daniel. The item is sound.

clues.clue: I was a Tishbite.
Ravens fed me by the brook Cherith.
I challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
I went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
clues.concern: Elisha was present at this event (2 Kings 2:11-12), but it was Elijah who went up, so the clue does not truly fit Elisha.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV and point uniquely to Elijah. The explanation matches 1 Kings 17:6. The hint 'Look in 1 Kings' is fine, though the whirlwind clue comes from 2 Kings 2:11.

clues.clue: I was one of the twelve spies.
clues.concern: Joshua (Oshea, Numbers 13:8), who is a listed option, was also one of the twelve spies, so this clue alone does not tell Caleb and Joshua apart.

clues.clue: I brought back a good report with Joshua.
clues.concern: The KJV never uses the exact phrase 'good report' for Caleb and Joshua. Numbers 13:32 uses 'evil report' for the other spies, and Numbers 14:7 has Joshua and Caleb calling it 'an exceeding good land.' The wording is a fair paraphrase. 'With Joshua' rules Joshua out.

clues.clue: I was eighty-five years old when I asked for my inheritance.
I asked for the mountain and received Hebron.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (one of the twelve spies) also fits Joshua (Numbers 13:8, 16). The later clues single out Caleb.
notes: The explanation matches Joshua 14:13: 'And Joshua blessed him, and gave unto Hebron unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh for an inheritance.' The reference label Joshua 14:6-13 covers clues 3 and 4 and alludes to the spying mission, but clues 1 and 2 are best supported in Numbers 13-14. Othniel and Phinehas do not fit any clue.

clues.clue: I was a prophetess.
clues.concern: Miriam (Exodus 15:20) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14) are also called prophetesses, so this clue alone fits two distractors. It is acceptable as an opening clue because the later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: I judged Israel under a palm tree in mount Ephraim.
clues.concern: Slight paraphrase. The KJV says she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el, and Israel came up to her for judgment. The meaning is substantially accurate.

clues.clue: I summoned Barak to fight Sisera.
A song of mine is recorded in Judges 5.
clues.concern: The song was sung by Deborah and Barak together (Judges 5:1), so 'a song of mine' slightly overstates sole ownership. Jael is also celebrated in the song (Judges 5:24-27), but she is not its singer, so this does not truly fit her.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('I was a prophetess') also fits Miriam (Exodus 15:20) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14). Clues 2-4 uniquely identify Deborah.
notes: The answer and explanation are accurate to Judges 4:4-5. Consider rewording clue 4 to 'Barak and I sang a song of victory' for precision. Also, citing Judges 5 in the clue, together with the hint 'Look in Judges,' makes the item quite easy for difficulty 3.

clues.clue: I walked with God.
clues.concern: Noah, a listed option, is also said to have 'walked with God' (Genesis 6:9), so this clue alone does not single out Enoch. The other clues resolve it.

clues.clue: I was the father of Methuselah.
I was not, for God took me.
clues.concern: Elijah was also taken up without dying (2 Kings 2:11), but this exact wording applies only to Enoch.

clues.clue: Hebrews says I was translated so I should not see death.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('I walked with God') also fits Noah (Genesis 6:9: 'Noah walked with God'). Clue 3 is thematically reminiscent of Elijah's translation (2 Kings 2:11), though its wording is unique to Enoch.
notes: The answer Enoch is correct and the clues taken together are unambiguous. The explanation accurately quotes Genesis 5:24, dropping only the initial 'And'. Consider rewording clue 1 to 'I walked with God after begetting Methuselah three hundred years' (Genesis 5:22) to avoid overlap with Noah.

clues.clue: I was ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen when I was called.
clues.concern: Minor: the KJV spells it 'plowing'. Elisha was with the twelfth yoke, and twelve yoke were 'before him'. The wording is acceptable.

clues.clue: I asked for a double portion of my master's spirit.
I took up the mantle that fell from Elijah.
I told Naaman to wash in the Jordan seven times.
clues.concern: Minor: Elisha gave this instruction through a messenger and did not meet Naaman in person. The messenger is unnamed, so the clue does not point to Gehazi, but 'sent word to' would be more precise.

notes: The answer, Elisha, is correct and every clue is supported by Scripture. The explanation accurately quotes 2 Kings 2:9. The hint 'Look in 2 Kings' covers three of the four clues, but clue 1 comes from 1 Kings 19:19. Consider changing 'ploughing' to the KJV spelling 'plowing' and noting that the Naaman instruction came through a messenger.

clues.clue: I was raised by my cousin Mordecai.
clues.concern: KJV says Mordecai 'brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter'. 'Cousin' is a correct inference but is not the KJV wording.

clues.clue: I became queen in Persia.
clues.concern: Also fits the distractor Vashti, who was queen before Esther (Esther 1:9). The other clues make the answer clear.

clues.clue: I said: If I perish, I perish.
The feast of Purim remembers my people's deliverance.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 ('I became queen in Persia') also fits Vashti, who was queen to Ahasuerus (Esther 1:9). Consider rewording it, e.g. 'I replaced Vashti as queen' (Esther 2:17).
notes: The answer and the explanation are accurate to Esther 4:16. The hint 'Look in Esther' gives away the answer outright. Consider a less revealing hint, such as 'Look in the book named after a Persian queen,' or simply accept it for difficulty 1.

clues.clue: An angel found me threshing wheat by a winepress.
I tested God with a fleece.
My army was reduced to three hundred men.
We carried trumpets, pitchers and lamps.

notes: All clues accurately reflect the KJV account of Gideon (Judges 6-7). Clue 1: KJV says Gideon 'threshed wheat by the winepress'. 'Found me' is a slight paraphrase: the angel 'came, and sat under an oak' and 'appeared unto him', but the sense is accurate. Clue 2: Judges 6:36-40 describes the two fleece tests. Clue 3: Judges 7:2-7 tells how the army was reduced to 300. Clue 4: Judges 7:16, 20 describes the trumpets, empty pitchers and lamps. None of the clues fits Joshua, Barak or Ehud. Joshua's men blew trumpets at Jericho (Joshua 6), but that involved no pitchers or lamps. The ref_kjv text matches Judges 7:7 in the KJV, and the explanation is accurate.

clues.clue: I was born holding my twin brother's heel.
I bought my brother's birthright with pottage.
I dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven.
God renamed me Israel.
clues.concern: The renaming is spoken by the one who wrestled with Jacob. Genesis 35:10 states explicitly that God renamed him. Either reference supports the clue.

notes: All clues uniquely identify Jacob. Esau is the twin whose heel was held and who sold the birthright, but the clues are framed from Jacob's perspective, so they do not fit Esau. The explanation quotes Genesis 32:28 accurately.

clues.clue: I was a cunning hunter.
clues.concern: Taken alone, this partly overlaps with Nimrod, 'a mighty hunter before the LORD' (Genesis 10:9). The KJV wording 'cunning hunter' is unique to Esau, so this is minor.

clues.clue: I was born red and hairy.
I sold my birthright for a meal.
I am also called Edom.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (hunter) could initially suggest Nimrod (Genesis 10:9), though 'cunning hunter' is specifically Esau's description. The later clues are unique to Esau.
notes: The answer is well supported. The cited Genesis 25:30-33 covers the Edom name and the sale of the birthright. Consider widening the cited range to Genesis 25:30-34, since verse 34 names the meal (bread and pottage of lentiles).

clues.clue: My husband was Elkanah.
clues.concern: This also fits the distractor Peninnah, Elkanah's other wife (1 Samuel 1:2). It does not uniquely identify Hannah, though later clues do.

clues.clue: I prayed silently at Shiloh, and Eli thought I was drunk.
I vowed to give my son to the LORD.
I named my son Samuel.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('My husband was Elkanah') also fits Peninnah, who was Elkanah's other wife (1 Samuel 1:2).
notes: Hannah is the correct answer, and clues 2-4 make it unique. The explanation matches 1 Samuel 1:20, which falls within the cited range 1 Samuel 1:13-20. Shiloh as the setting is established in 1 Samuel 1:3 and 1:9. Consider rewording clue 1 (e.g. 'My husband Elkanah loved me though I was barren') so it does not also fit Peninnah, or accept it as a deliberately ambiguous opening clue.

clues.clue: I saw the Lord high and lifted up in the year King Uzziah died.
A seraph touched my lips with a live coal.
I answered: Here am I; send me.
I prophesied of a child called Immanuel.
clues.concern: Micah 5:2-3 also foretells a coming ruler born of a woman in travail, but only Isaiah gives the name Immanuel, so this is not a real conflict.

notes: All clues are accurate to the KJV. In Isaiah 6:7 the seraph lays the coal on Isaiah's mouth and says 'this hath touched thy lips.' The hint 'Look in Isaiah' gives away the answer outright, since the book name matches the correct option. It should be revised, for example to 'Look in the vision of the temple in the year a king died.'

clues.clue: God said He knew me before He formed me in the belly.
I protested that I was only a child.
I was let down into a dungeon full of mire.
clues.concern: KJV says the dungeon had 'no water, but mire' and that Jeremiah 'sunk in the mire'. 'Full of mire' is a slight paraphrase, but it is acceptable.

clues.clue: Baruch wrote my words on a roll.

notes: Every clue is specific to Jeremiah. Isaiah 49:1,5 speaks of being called or formed from the womb, but that refers to the Servant, and the 'knew thee' wording is unique to Jeremiah 1:5. The explanation quotes the reference accurately and correctly labels 'weeping prophet' as tradition. A possible minor wording improvement for clue 3: 'I sank in the mire of a dungeon.'

clues.clue: I lived in the land of Uz.
I was perfect and upright.
I lost my children and possessions in a single day.
I said: The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away.

notes: All clues are accurate and point uniquely to Job. Eliphaz is a Temanite (Job 2:11), Bildad a Shuhite (Job 2:11), and Elihu a Buzite (Job 32:2), so none is said to live in Uz. Clue 3 is supported by Job 1:13, where all the calamities come on 'a day' while the children feast, with the messengers arriving in quick succession through verse 19. The explanation correctly quotes Job 1:21. Minor point: the hint 'Look in Job' gives little help, since all four options appear in the book of Job, and the book's title gives away the answer anyway.

clues.clue: My father Zacharias was a priest.
I wore raiment of camel's hair.
clues.concern: Minor: Elijah is described as 'an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather' (2 Kings 1:8), but camel's hair is not specified for him, so the clue still points to John.

clues.clue: I ate locusts and wild honey.
I baptized Jesus in the Jordan.

notes: All clues are accurate in the KJV. Clue 1 is supported by Luke 1:5 ('a certain priest named Zacharias'), with Luke 1:13 confirming he is John's father. Clue 4 is supported by Mark 1:9 and Matthew 3:13-16. The explanation matches Matthew 3:4. The hint 'Look in Matthew' is fine, though clue 1 comes only from Luke.

clues.clue: I was a son of Zebedee.
clues.concern: Also fits the distractor James, who was likewise a son of Zebedee.

clues.clue: Jesus surnamed my brother and me Boanerges.
clues.concern: Also fits James, who received the same surname together with John.

clues.clue: Tradition identifies me as the disciple whom Jesus loved.
clues.concern: Scripture never names the beloved disciple, so this identification rests on tradition. The clue honestly labels it as tradition, but it is not a textual fact.

clues.clue: I was on the isle of Patmos for the word of God.
clues.concern: The text names only 'John'. Identifying this John with the apostle and son of Zebedee is traditional, not stated in Scripture.

distractor_conflict: James fits clues 1 and 2: he was a son of Zebedee (Matthew 4:21) and shared the name Boanerges (Mark 3:17).
notes: The answer John is the intended and standard answer. The only clues that separate John from James are clues 3 and 4, and both depend on traditional identifications (the beloved disciple, and the apostle as author of Revelation) rather than explicit text. The explanation correctly quotes Revelation 1:9 and openly acknowledges that the authorship identification is traditional. This is acceptable for difficulty 2. Consider adding a clue that is explicitly textual and unique to John, such as being sent with Peter to prepare the passover (Luke 22:8) or going up to the temple with Peter (Acts 3:1).

clues.clue: I was a prophet, the son of Amittai.
clues.concern: Jonah 1:1 names him as son of Amittai but does not call him a prophet; 2 Kings 14:25 supplies both details.

clues.clue: I fled from God's call on a ship.
I spent three days inside a great fish.
clues.concern: KJV says 'three days and three nights'; the clue is accurate but abbreviated.

clues.clue: I was displeased when Nineveh repented.
clues.concern: Strictly, Jonah was displeased that God spared Nineveh (Jonah 3:10) after its repentance. This is acceptable.

notes: The answer and explanation match Jonah 1:1. Nahum also prophesied concerning Nineveh, but none of the clues fit him. The hint 'Look in Jonah' gives away the answer outright, which may be too revealing even at difficulty 1. Consider citing 2 Kings 14:25 for the 'prophet' detail.

clues.clue: I was one of the twelve.
clues.concern: Also fits Peter, Thomas, and Andrew (all of the twelve), but subsequent clues disambiguate; acceptable as an opening clue.

clues.clue: I had the bag.
I agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
I betrayed Jesus with a kiss.

notes: Answer and explanation are accurate to Matthew 26:14-15. The first clue alone fits all options, but later clues uniquely identify Judas. The 'bag' clue comes from John 12:6 and John 13:29, not Matthew. The hint 'Look in Matthew' is still adequate because clues 3-4 are in Matthew.

clues.clue: I was my father's favourite son.
clues.concern: KJV says Israel 'loved Joseph more than all his children'. 'Favourite' is a fair paraphrase. Benjamin was also specially loved later (Genesis 44:20), but the clue is clearly Joseph's.

clues.clue: My brothers sold me into slavery.
clues.concern: KJV says they 'sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver'. The word 'slavery' is not in the verse, but Genesis 45:4 ('whom ye sold into Egypt') and Psalms 105:17 ('sold for a servant') support it. Some readers note that Midianite merchants drew him out of the pit, but Genesis 45:4 confirms the brothers' agency.

clues.clue: I interpreted Pharaoh's dreams.
I was set over all the land of Egypt.

notes: The clues together uniquely identify Joseph. Moses was raised in Pharaoh's house but did not interpret dreams and was not set over Egypt. Benjamin was loved by his father but was not sold. The explanation quotes Genesis 41:41 accurately.

clues.clue: I was one of twelve men sent to spy out Canaan.
clues.concern: This clue also fits the distractor Caleb (Numbers 13:6). In Numbers 13:8 Joshua is listed as 'Oshea the son of Nun'; he is renamed in Numbers 13:16. The clue is acceptable only because later clues disambiguate.

clues.clue: I succeeded Moses as leader.
The walls of Jericho fell when the people shouted.
clues.concern: This is not phrased in the first person, unlike the other clues, and does not state Joshua's role directly. The fact itself is accurate.

clues.clue: I said: As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 also fits Caleb, who was one of the twelve spies (Numbers 13:6), but the remaining clues uniquely identify Joshua.
notes: The answer is correct and the explanation quotes Joshua 24:15 accurately. Consider rewording clue 1 so it does not equally fit Caleb, for example 'one of only two spies who brought a good report' still fits Caleb, so a clue tied to Joshua's renaming (Numbers 13:16) may be better. Consider rephrasing clue 3 in the first person, for example 'At my command the people shouted and Jericho's walls fell' (Joshua 6:16, 20).

clues.clue: I lived in Nazareth of Galilee.
The angel Gabriel was sent to me.
clues.concern: Gabriel also appeared to Zacharias (Luke 1:19), Elisabeth's husband, but he was not sent to Elisabeth herself, so there is no real conflict.

clues.clue: I was espoused to Joseph.
I gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem.

notes: All clues are accurate and uniquely identify Mary. Elisabeth, Martha and Anna do not fit any clue. The explanation matches Luke 1:26-27. The Bethlehem birth is supported by Luke 2:4-7 (also Matthew 2:1).

clues.clue: I was a seller of purple.
I came from the city of Thyatira.
I heard Paul speak by a riverside at Philippi.
clues.concern: The riverside setting at Philippi comes from Acts 16:12-13, not from the cited 16:14-15. It is accurate.

clues.clue: My household was baptized.
clues.concern: Household baptisms also occur for the Philippian jailer and Stephanas, but neither is among the options, so there is no conflict.

notes: The answer and explanation are accurate. Consider expanding reference_label to Acts 16:13-15 so it covers the riverside detail. None of the distractors fit any clue: Dorcas (Acts 9), Priscilla (Acts 18) and Phebe (Romans 16:1).

clues.clue: I lived in Bethany with my sister and brother.
clues.concern: Luke 10:38 only says 'a certain village'. Bethany and the brother Lazarus come from John 11:1 (see also John 11:5, 12:1-2), which lies outside the cited reference.

clues.clue: I was cumbered about much serving.
Jesus said my sister had chosen the good part.
clues.concern: The KJV reads 'Mary hath chosen that good part', not 'the good part'. The verse is also outside the reference_label range (Luke 10:38-41).

clues.clue: I welcomed Jesus into my house.

notes: Martha is clearly correct, and no clue fits Mary Magdalene, Salome, or Joanna. The explanation accurately quotes Luke 10:40. Suggested fixes: extend reference_label to Luke 10:38-42 so it covers clue 3, or add John 11:1 for clue 1. Optionally change clue 3 to the KJV wording 'that good part'.

clues.clue: I lived in Bethany.
clues.concern: This also fits the distractor 'Simon'. Simon the leper lived in Bethany (Matthew 26:6; Mark 14:3). The later clues still make the answer unambiguous.

clues.clue: My sisters were Mary and Martha.
Jesus wept near my grave.
clues.concern: This is slightly imprecise. Jesus wept after asking 'Where have ye laid him?' (John 11:34-35), and only afterward 'cometh to the grave' (John 11:38). So he wept on the way to the grave rather than strictly at it. 'Near' is defensible but loose.

clues.clue: Jesus called me out of the tomb.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('I lived in Bethany') also fits Simon. Simon the leper hosted Jesus at his house in Bethany (Matthew 26:6; Mark 14:3). The remaining clues uniquely identify Lazarus.
notes: The answer and the explanation match John 11:43-44 accurately. Consider rewording clue 3 to 'Jesus wept when he came to raise me' or simply 'Jesus wept for me' to match John 11:35 more exactly. Optionally, replace the 'Simon' distractor, or make the Bethany clue more specific, to avoid the overlap with Simon the leper.

clues.clue: Seven devils had gone out of me.
clues.concern: Mark 16:9 states the same.

clues.clue: I stood by the cross.
clues.concern: Not unique on its own. John 19:25 also names Mary the wife of Cleophas, whom many identify with Mary the mother of James. Mark 15:40 places Mary the mother of James and Salome 'afar off' watching the crucifixion. The remaining clues still make the answer unique.

clues.clue: I came to the tomb while it was yet dark.
At first I supposed the risen Jesus was the gardener.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 alone could partially fit Mary the mother of James (if she is identified with Mary the wife of Cleophas, John 19:25) or Salome (Mark 15:40, beholding afar off). Clues 1 and 4 apply only to Mary Magdalene, so the item as a whole is not ambiguous.
notes: Accurate item. The reference John 20:15-16 matches the quoted KJV text and the explanation. Clue 2 is the weakest clue but is acceptable in combination with the others. The hint 'Look in John' fits clues 2-4; clue 1 comes from Luke and Mark.

clues.clue: My father was Enoch.
My son was Lamech.
clues.concern: Minor: another Lamech (son of Methusael, Cain's line) appears in Genesis 4:18, but the clue fits Methuselah only.

clues.clue: I was Noah's grandfather.
clues.concern: Inferred from Genesis 5:25 plus 5:28-29 rather than stated in a single verse, but it is a valid inference.

clues.clue: I lived nine hundred sixty and nine years.

notes: The answer is correct. No clue fits Mahalaleel, Jared, or Enoch. Jared was Enoch's father and Methuselah's grandfather, so he is not Noah's grandfather. Enoch is Methuselah's father, not a son of Enoch, so he is clearly excluded. The explanation quotes Genesis 5:27 accurately.

clues.clue: I was king of Salem.
I was priest of the most high God.
clues.concern: Aaron and Jethro were also priests, but neither is called 'priest of the most high God'. The clue only partly overlaps with those distractors and is not decisive alone.

clues.clue: I brought forth bread and wine to Abram.
clues.concern: Genesis 14:18 says only 'brought forth bread and wine'. The recipient (Abram) is implied by context (14:17-19) rather than stated in the verse. This is acceptable.

clues.clue: Abram gave me tithes of all.
clues.concern: In Genesis 14:20 the pronouns are ambiguous ('he gave him tithes of all'). Hebrews 7:2 and 7:4 make clear that Abraham gave the tenth to Melchizedek. Citing Hebrews 7:2 alongside would strengthen the clue.

notes: The answer Melchizedek is correct and well supported by Genesis 14:18-20, and Hebrews 7:1-4 corroborates it. The distractors are Abimelech (king of Gerar), Aaron (priest) and Jethro (priest of Midian), and none fits all the clues. The explanation is accurate but covers only one clue; it could also mention the tithes, citing Hebrews 7:2. Difficulty 4 seems high, since the first clue ('king of Salem') gives the answer away immediately; consider lowering the difficulty or reordering the clues so the less specific ones come first.

clues.clue: I was a publican.
clues.concern: This also fits the distractor Zacchaeus, who was 'chief among the publicans' (Luke 19:2).

clues.clue: I sat at the receipt of custom.
Jesus said to me: Follow me.
clues.concern: Jesus also said 'Follow me' to others, such as Philip in John 1:43, though none of the other options received this call in this setting.

clues.clue: Jesus ate with publicans and sinners at my table.
clues.concern: Matthew 9:10 says only 'in the house' and does not name the host. Luke 5:29 (Levi's 'own house') and Mark 2:15 ('his house') make the host explicit, under the name Levi. The clue partly overlaps Zacchaeus, at whose house Jesus was a guest amid murmuring that he was 'a sinner' (Luke 19:5-7), though no gathering of publicans and sinners is described there.

distractor_conflict: Zacchaeus fits clue 1: he was a chief publican (Luke 19:2). He partly fits clue 4: Jesus ate at his house (Luke 19:5-7). Only clues 2 and 3 clearly separate Matthew from Zacchaeus.
notes: The answer Matthew is correct when the clues are read together. Consider making clue 1 more specific, for example 'I am called Matthew the publican in the list of the twelve' (Matthew 10:3), or reordering the clues so the publican clue does not lead toward Zacchaeus. Clue 4 is best supported by Luke 5:29 or Mark 2:15, which name the host as Levi, rather than by Matthew 9:10.

clues.clue: I watched over my baby brother at the river.
clues.concern: The sister is unnamed in Exodus 2:4-8. Identifying her as Miriam is a reasonable inference: Numbers 26:59 names Miriam as the only sister of Moses and Aaron. The text does not explicitly state it.

clues.clue: I am called a prophetess.
clues.concern: This also fits the distractor Deborah, whom Judges 4:4 calls a prophetess. The clue is not decisive on its own, but the other clues settle the answer.

clues.clue: I led the women with a timbrel after the Red Sea crossing.
I was briefly struck with leprosy.
clues.concern: 'Briefly' is supported by Numbers 12:14-15, where she is shut out of the camp for seven days.

distractor_conflict: Deborah is also called a prophetess (Judges 4:4), so clue 2 alone fits her. The other clues exclude her.
notes: The answer and explanation match Exodus 15:20 KJV. Clue 1 depends on identifying the unnamed sister of Exodus 2 as Miriam, which is reasonable but inferred. The hint 'Look in Exodus' covers most clues, but the leprosy clue comes from Numbers 12.

clues.clue: I was cupbearer to King Artaxerxes.
clues.concern: Nehemiah 1:11 says 'I was the king's cupbearer'; the king is named as Artaxerxes in Nehemiah 2:1. Both verses together fully support the clue.

clues.clue: I wept over Jerusalem's broken walls.
I led the rebuilding of the city wall.
The wall was finished in fifty-two days.

notes: Every clue fits Nehemiah uniquely. Ezra also served under Artaxerxes (Ezra 7), but he is not called a cupbearer. Zerubbabel and Haggai were tied to rebuilding the temple, not the wall. The explanation correctly quotes Nehemiah 6:15. The hint 'Look in Nehemiah' nearly gives away the answer, but that is a design matter, not an accuracy problem.

clues.clue: I was captain of the host of the king of Syria.
I was a leper.
clues.concern: On its own this also fits Gehazi, who was struck with Naaman's leprosy (2 Kings 5:27). The other clues still make the answer unambiguous.

clues.clue: A captive little maid from Israel told of a prophet.
clues.concern: Minor: this is not phrased in the first person like the other clues. The maid spoke to Naaman's wife about the prophet in Samaria, and Naaman did not hear her directly, though it was reported to him (5:4).

clues.clue: I dipped myself seven times in the Jordan.
clues.concern: Minor: the KJV reads 'in Jordan', not 'the Jordan'.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 ('I was a leper') also fits Gehazi (2 Kings 5:27), but the combined clues identify only Naaman.
notes: The answer and the cited reference are accurate. The explanation matches 2 Kings 5:14, though it could add 'and he was clean' for completeness. Consider using the first person in clue 3 (e.g., 'A captive little maid from Israel in my house spoke of a prophet') for consistency.

clues.clue: I was a fisherman, the brother of Andrew.
Jesus called me to become a fisher of men.
clues.concern: The call was addressed to both Peter and Andrew, so this clue alone also fits the distractor Andrew. The item is still uniquely resolved by the other clues.

clues.clue: I walked on the water toward Jesus.
I denied Jesus three times before the cock crew.

distractor_conflict: Clue 2 (fisher of men) also fits Andrew per Matthew 4:19. Clue 1 implicitly excludes Andrew by naming him as the brother.
notes: The answer Peter is correct. The explanation accurately quotes the KJV of Matthew 26:75. In Matthew 4:18, Peter is named as 'Simon called Peter.' This is a minor clue overlap only; it is acceptable at difficulty 1.

clues.clue: As a baby I was hidden in an ark of bulrushes.
clues.concern: Strictly, he was hidden for three months (Exodus 2:2) and then placed in the ark of bulrushes among the flags (Exodus 2:3). Calling the ark itself a hiding place is a fair paraphrase.

clues.clue: I was raised in Pharaoh's household.
clues.concern: Scripture says he became the son of Pharaoh's daughter, and Acts 7:21 says she 'nourished him for her own son.' 'Pharaoh's household' is an acceptable paraphrase. Joseph was set over Pharaoh's house as an adult (Genesis 41:40), but he was not raised there, so this is only a slight overlap.

clues.clue: I saw a bush burn without being consumed.
I led Israel out of Egypt.
clues.concern: Aaron is named alongside Moses in bringing Israel out (Exodus 6:26-27), and Joshua was present. Moses is clearly the principal leader, and the earlier clues are unique to him.

notes: The item is accurate. The cited Exodus 3:2-4 supports the burning bush clue, and the explanation matches verse 4. The clue set as a whole uniquely identifies Moses. There are only minor partial overlaps: Aaron shared in leading Israel out (Exodus 6:26-27), and Joseph was over Pharaoh's house as an adult.

clues.clue: I lived before a great flood.
clues.concern: Vague. Enoch, a distractor, also lived before the flood (Genesis 5:21-24). Noah also lived through and after the flood (Genesis 9:28), so 'lived before' undersells him. The later clues resolve this.

clues.clue: God told me to build with gopher wood.
My sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.
I built the ark.
clues.concern: Genesis 6:22 also supports this indirectly ('Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him'). Hebrews 11:7 states it explicitly: 'prepared an ark'.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 ('I lived before a great flood') also fits Enoch, who lived before the flood (Genesis 5:21-24).
notes: The answer, Noah, is correct and the explanation matches Genesis 6:14 in the KJV. Clue 1 is the only weak clue: it fits Enoch as well. Consider rewording it, e.g. 'I lived through a great flood' (Genesis 7:6, 7:23). The clues as a set uniquely identify Noah.

clues.clue: I was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews.
clues.concern: Taken alone, this partly overlaps with Gamaliel, a Pharisee (Acts 5:34), and with Joseph of Arimathaea, a counsellor (Luke 23:50). Neither is called 'a ruler of the Jews' in those words, though, and the full set of clues points only to Nicodemus.

clues.clue: I came to Jesus by night.
Jesus told me I must be born again.
clues.concern: The word 'must' matches John 3:7 ('Ye must be born again') exactly. John 3:3 gives the related wording 'Except a man be born again.'

clues.clue: I brought myrrh and aloes for Jesus' burial.
clues.concern: Joseph of Arimathaea was also involved in the burial (John 19:38). However, the myrrh and aloes are attributed specifically to Nicodemus, so the clue is accurate.

notes: The answer, Nicodemus, is correct and well supported. The explanation accurately quotes John 3:3, which falls within the cited John 3:1-3. Two optional improvements: extend reference_label to cover John 3:7 and John 19:39, since the 'must' wording and the burial clue come from those verses. Joseph of Arimathaea appears alongside Nicodemus in John 19:38-40, but only Nicodemus is said to bring the myrrh and aloes, so the distractor is not defensible.

clues.clue: I was born in Tarsus.
I once persecuted the church.
A light from heaven blinded me near Damascus.
clues.concern: Acts 9:3 mentions the light; the blindness is stated in Acts 9:8-9 and attributed to the light in Acts 22:11.

clues.clue: I wrote many letters to the churches.
clues.concern: Scripture does not literally say 'many letters'. Peter speaks of 'all his epistles', and the letters' authorship is shown by their openings (e.g., Romans 1:1). The clue is acceptable as a summary.

notes: Paul is the correct answer. No distractor fits any clue: Barnabas was from Cyprus (Acts 4:36), Stephen was martyred (Acts 7), and Silas was Paul's companion. The cited Acts 9:3-4 supports the light and the voice but not the blinding (Acts 9:8-9), so consider expanding the reference to Acts 9:3-9. The explanation's statement that he is later called Paul is supported by Acts 13:9.

clues.clue: My house was upon the town wall of Jericho.
I hid two Israelite spies.
I let them down by a cord through a window.
A line of scarlet thread marked my home.
clues.concern: Minor: the text says the thread was bound in the window as the agreed sign (Joshua 2:18, 21). 'Marked my home' is a fair paraphrase.

notes: All clues are directly supported by Joshua 2. She bound the scarlet line in the window in Joshua 2:21. None of the distractors fit: Jael killed Sisera in a tent, Deborah was a judge, and Ruth was a Moabitess. The explanation matches Joshua 2:18. The ref_kjv excerpt is truncated, but it is consistent with the passage.

clues.clue: I was a Nazarite from birth.
clues.concern: Minor: KJV says 'from my mother's womb' (also Judges 13:5, 'from the womb'). This is slightly earlier than birth, but the meaning is equivalent.

clues.clue: I tore a young lion with my bare hands.
Delilah learned the secret of my strength.
I pulled down the house where the Philistines gathered.
clues.concern: Minor: KJV describes him taking hold of the two middle pillars and bowing himself so that the house fell. 'Pulled down' is a fair paraphrase.

notes: Every clue is uniquely true of Samson. None applies to Gideon, Saul, or Jephthah. The explanation accurately reflects Judges 16:30. The item is accurate and suitable for difficulty 1.

clues.clue: I was a woman of Moab.
clues.concern: Also fits Orpah, who is named in the same verse as a Moabite wife. Ruth 1:22 ('Ruth the Moabitess') is specific to Ruth.

clues.clue: I told my mother-in-law: whither thou goest, I will go.
I gleaned in the fields of Boaz.
I became an ancestor of King David.
clues.concern: Also fits Rahab, who is listed as Boaz's mother in David's line (Matthew 1:5-6). Matthew 1:5 names Ruth as well.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (woman of Moab) also fits Orpah (Ruth 1:4). Clue 4 (ancestor of David) also fits Rahab (Matthew 1:5). Clues 2 and 3 make the combined set identify only Ruth.
notes: The answer Ruth is correct, and the explanation matches Ruth 1:16. Two clues taken alone also fit a distractor, but the full set is unambiguous. Consider rewording clue 1 to 'I was called the Moabitess' (Ruth 1:22) and clue 4 to 'I was the great-grandmother of King David' (Ruth 4:17) to sharpen it.

clues.clue: My mother Hannah prayed for me at Shiloh.
clues.concern: Hannah's prayer at Shiloh is in 1 Samuel 1:9-11, and her naming of Samuel is in 1 Samuel 1:20. The KJV places the prayer in the temple of the LORD at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1:3, 9).

clues.clue: As a boy I served Eli the priest.
clues.concern: The KJV wording is that the child Samuel 'ministered unto the LORD before Eli' (also 1 Samuel 2:11). Saying he served Eli is a reasonable paraphrase.

clues.clue: I heard the LORD call my name in the night.
I anointed both Saul and David.
clues.concern: Saul's anointing is in 1 Samuel 10:1, and David's is in 1 Samuel 16:13. No single verse covers both.

notes: The answer, Samuel, is correct, and all clues are accurate to the KJV. Eli fits clue 2 only as the priest Samuel served, not as the speaker. Nathan and Gad do not fit any clue. The explanation matches the cited verse, 1 Samuel 3:10. Clue 1 gives the answer away almost immediately, which is acceptable for difficulty 2.

clues.clue: I was of the tribe of Benjamin.
clues.concern: Also true of Jonathan, Saul's son, though the later clues rule him out.

clues.clue: From my shoulders upward I was higher than any of the people.
Samuel anointed me as Israel's first king.
clues.concern: The KJV never uses the words 'first king', but this is clearly implied by 1 Samuel 8-10.

clues.clue: I consulted a woman at Endor.
clues.concern: Accurate, though the clue omits that she had a familiar spirit (1 Samuel 28:7).

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (tribe of Benjamin) also fits Jonathan, but the other clues identify Saul uniquely.
notes: Saul is the correct answer. The explanation closely matches the KJV wording of 1 Samuel 9:2. Saul's height is also noted in 1 Samuel 10:23. Saul's Benjamite lineage is also given in 1 Samuel 9:1 (Kish, a Benjamite).

clues.clue: My mother was Bathsheba.
I asked God for an understanding heart.
I built the temple in Jerusalem.
clues.concern: David prepared materials and planned the temple (1 Chronicles 22), but Scripture says Solomon built it, so the clue does not fit David.

clues.clue: I judged between two women who both claimed one baby.

notes: All clues are well supported by the KJV. The ref_kjv text matches 1 Kings 3:10-12 accurately, and the explanation's quotation ('a wise and an understanding heart') appears in verse 12. None of the distractors fit the clues: Rehoboam's mother was Naamah (1 Kings 14:21), Hezekiah's mother was Abi (2 Kings 18:2), and David did not build the temple (1 Kings 5:3-5).

clues.clue: I was one of the twelve, called Didymus.
I was absent when Jesus first appeared to the disciples.
clues.concern: Slightly imprecise: Thomas was absent at Jesus' first appearance to the gathered disciples (John 20:19-24). Jesus had already appeared to Mary Magdalene (John 20:14-18), to Peter (Luke 24:34), and to the two on the Emmaus road (Luke 24:13-31). Acceptable in context.

clues.clue: I wanted to see the print of the nails.
I said: My Lord and my God.

notes: All clues point uniquely to Thomas. 'Didymus' alone identifies him (John 11:16; 20:24; 21:2). The explanation matches John 20:28 KJV. One optional improvement: reword the second clue to 'when Jesus came to the disciples on the evening of the first day.'

clues.clue: I was one of seven chosen to serve the church.
clues.concern: This clue also fits Philip, a distractor, who was likewise one of the seven (Acts 6:5). The text says they were appointed to 'serve tables' (Acts 6:2), which is narrower than 'serve the church'.

clues.clue: I was full of faith and power.
As I spoke I saw the heavens opened.
I was stoned while a young man named Saul watched.
clues.concern: The text says the witnesses laid their clothes at Saul's feet and that he was consenting (Acts 8:1; 22:20). 'Watched' is a fair paraphrase.

distractor_conflict: Clue 1 (one of the seven) also fits Philip (Acts 6:5).
notes: The answer Stephen is correct and clearly identified by clues 2-4. Clue 1 alone does not distinguish Stephen from Philip, but the full clue set resolves it. Consider rewording clue 1 to say 'serve tables', or accept it as an intentionally broad opening clue.

clues.clue: I was chief among the publicans.
clues.concern: Matthew was also a publican (Matthew 10:3), though not called chief. With this clue alone a player might think of Matthew, but 'chief' distinguishes Zacchaeus.

clues.clue: I was rich.
clues.concern: Nicodemus could arguably be inferred wealthy (John 19:39), but Scripture never calls him rich. Generic on its own.

clues.clue: I was little of stature.
I climbed a sycomore tree to see Jesus.

notes: The item is accurate and the clues match Luke 19:2-4 in the KJV. Early clues partially overlap with Matthew (a publican), but the combination of clues uniquely identifies Zacchaeus. The KJV spells the name 'Zacchæus'.

clues.clue: My grandmother Lois and mother Eunice shared unfeigned faith.
I was Paul's young companion.
clues.concern: Acts 16:1-3 establishes him as Paul's companion. His youth is from 1 Timothy 4:12 ('Let no man despise thy youth'). The clue is vague on its own: Titus, Silas, and Luke were also Paul's companions, though 'young' points to Timothy. Later clues resolve it.

clues.clue: Paul called me his dearly beloved son.
clues.concern: Titus is also called 'mine own son after the common faith' (Titus 1:4), but the exact phrase 'dearly beloved son' is used only of Timothy.

clues.clue: Two New Testament letters are addressed to me.
clues.concern: Both letters are addressed to Timothy: 1 Timothy 1:2 and 2 Timothy 1:2. Titus has only one letter, so this clue is unique to Timothy.

notes: The answer is correct and the reference text matches the KJV. The 'young companion' clue is weak and should be supported by Acts 16:1-3 together with 1 Timothy 4:12. The explanation accurately reflects 2 Timothy 1:5.
